messages:
IncidentBot: :rotating_light: Alert: spike in KMS API 5xx and client timeouts seen from service-startup path in us-central1. 120+ startup failures across prod clusters in the last 3m
Alex G: got paged, looking
Alex G: paging oncall (Maria) now @Maria R
Maria R: taking it. first pass: are services failing healthchecks or crashing on startup?
Jamal S: crashes on init, logs show signing errors when contacting Cloud KMS for key unwrap. example from app-logger:```
2026-03-15T12:34:21Z ERROR KMSClient - getKey failed. status=503 body=Service Unavailable
com.google.api.client.http.HttpResponseException: 503 Service Unavailable
Caused by: java.net.SocketTimeoutException: Read timed out
 at com.company.kms.KmsSigner.getKey(KmsSigner.java:128)

2026-03-15T12:34:22Z WARN Startup - unable to complete key handshake, aborting startup
```
Emily C: metrics show KMS external latency spike starting ~12:30, p50->p99 jump 200ms->4s and error rate to 10%
Alex G: confirmed restarts increasing; rolling deploys are amplifying. Some nodes in dedicated pools are stuck in CrashLoopBackOff
Maria R: immediate mitigations: 1) stop automated rolling restarts, 2) mark critical services as manual to avoid repeated restarts, 3) enable local cached-key fallback on new instances if available
Jamal S: can we flip the in-app fallback flag? quick patch available in config service: `KMS_FALLBACK=cache`
Maria R: applying to prod-critical namespace now. executing:`kubectl patch deploy config-service -n prod -p '{"spec":{"template":{"metadata":{"annotations":{"manual-deploy":"true"}}}}}'`
IncidentBot: @Maria R acknowledged and assigned to page rotation (oncall)
CloudProviderSupport: Thanks for the ping — we see elevated KMS control-plane latencies in us-central1 due to an internal routing issue. Engineers are investigating, ticket CP-8672 opened. ETA unclear.
Emily C: adding provider message to incident timeline
Alex G: rolling a targeted restart for nodes that already have cached keys; avoid reinitializing KMS handshake. doing `kubectl rollout restart` for subset (batch size 5)
Jamal S: temporary workaround: set env `SKIP_KMS_ON_INIT=true` for worker-startup path so they defer KMS unwrap until after startup and fallback to cached material if present
Maria R: implemented SKIP_KMS_ON_INIT in prod-critical (canary 10 instances) — monitoring for startup success
Alex G: can we also reduce concurrency for other rollouts? throttling CI/CD to avoid mass restarts. pinging DevEx to hold pipelines
Emily C: alerting severity updated to P1. customer-facing SRE notified to prepare status update
CloudProviderSupport: update: regional routing fix being tested, some recovery observed but error rate still elevated. We'll post when fully mitigated.
Maria R: Customer impact: services dependent on KMS unwrap at boot failed to become Ready; this led to degraded API endpoints for a subset of customers (approx 7% of active traffic routed through affected instances). No customer data exposure.
Jamal S: posting snippet of svc health check errors for visibility:```
GET /health 500 {"error":"signing_failed","code":"KMS_UNAVAILABLE"}
```
Alex G: putting together short status for status.redwood.ai — need exact impacted services list from service registry
Emily C: pulling service names now, will attach to status. metrics show request latency spike for auth and token exchange endpoints
Maria R: contacting account rep and cloud trust contact. cc @CloudProviderSupport — please escalate in CP-8672 as cross-region routing bug affecting KMS endpoints, any detail about expected time to full recovery?
CloudProviderSupport: Escalation acknowledged; providing Slack channel with assigned on-call in CP infra. Initial estimate: 30-90 minutes depending on propagation. We will post updates in this thread and in CP-8672.
Alex G: alerting Customer Success to expect inbound tickets and prepare templated message: short explanation + mitigation + ETA once cloud confirms
IncidentBot: Pager rotation changed — next oncall will be Jamal S in 25m (auto-handoff scheduled)
Maria R: prepping handoff notes for the oncoming shift: include what was done, what remains, and any commands to revert quick flags. Drafting now.
Jamal S: taking notes, will pickup in 20m. If provider hasn't resolved by then we'll consider controlled failover to secondary region and/or temporary KMS proxy in our VPC using cached key material (requires security review)
Maria R: agreed. next steps: 1) wait for CloudProviderSupport confirmation of full recovery, 2) if not recovered within 45m, prepare controlled failover runbook and brief security.
Alex G: adding reduced blast radius doc link: https://confluence.redwood.ai/ops/kms-fallbacks (for ops)
Emily C: added timeline to incident log: started 2026-03-15T12:30Z, provider notified 12:36Z, mitigations applied 12:40-12:55Z, partial recovery signs at 13:00Z
Maria R: Handoff summary for next oncall (Jamal S):
- Root cause: upstream KMS API control-plane latencies/routing errors in us-central1 causing 503s/timeouts during key unwrap at service startup
- Impact: ~7% of traffic degraded, multiple services in CrashLoopBackOff on startup; no data leakage detected
- Actions taken: stopped automated rollouts, applied SKIP_KMS_ON_INIT and KMS_FALLBACK=cache in critical namespaces, targeted restarts for nodes with cached keys, notified CloudProviderSupport and Account reps, updated public status page (draft), throttled CI/CD
- Commands & rollbacks: `kubectl set env deploy/<svc> -n prod SKIP_KMS_ON_INIT=true` to enable; revert by removing env or setting to false. To re-enable rollouts: `kubectl annotate deployment <svc> manual-deploy-`
- Outstanding: provider fix confirmation, validate no residual crashes once latency normalizes, prepare failover runbook if provider can't resolve within SLA window

Maria R: handing off to Jamal S at 13:05Z — please escalate to Sec if you propose using cached key proxy (security review required)
Jamal S: acknowledged, taking over. will monitor provider updates and post progress.
Maria R: thanks team — logging final note and closing active paging for this rotation. will follow-up with full postmortem once provider root cause is released. :white_check_mark:
